title: Operator continuity and knowledge succession playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Operator Continuity and Knowledge Succession program used by Platform Operators and SREs to ensure uninterrupted operational coverage, reduce cognitive load during shift handoffs, and retain tribal knowledge when individuals rotate, leave, or are unavailable. It contains a runbook-style checklist, handoff protocol, artifact catalog, training cadence, and a lightweight roadmap for continuous improvement.

Audience:
- Platform operators
- On-call SREs
- Team leads and managers
- Incident commanders and postmortem owners

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce mean handoff time (time to reach full context after a shift change) to < 15 minutes for Tier 1 incidents.
- Achieve 90% completion rate for pre-shift checklist within 10 minutes before shift start.
- Ensure each operator has at least 2 documented runbook-authority entries for critical services.

Scope:
- Applies to platform-level services in the eng-platform ownership surface: routing/orchestration, KV-prefix cache, batch/queueing, tenant-slicing controllers, and operator tooling.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks owned by downstream service owners; instead, links to them and codifies operator-level escalation and fallback behaviors.

Operator roles and ownership:
- Primary Operator: first responder for the oncall shift, owns initial triage and communication.
- Secondary (Runner): acts as backup for escalations and carries out longer-term remediation tasks.
- Shift Lead: for multi-shift incidents (cross-region), coordinates cross-shift continuity.
- Knowledge Steward: appointed for each critical subsystem; responsible for maintaining canonical docs and running quarterly knowledge transfer sessions.

Roster & Succession rules:
1. Every rotation must have a designated Primary, Secondary, and Shift Lead documented in the oncall roster board.
2. The Knowledge Steward for a subsystem must not be the only person listed as an expert; at least two deputies must be named.
3. If a Knowledge Steward departs, the team lead must nominate replacements within 7 calendar days.

Pre-shift checklist (to be completed in the 10 minutes before taking Primary):
- Verify pager and Slack contact routing. (CLI: /oncall status)
- Confirm alarms assigned: open the team dashboard and ensure no unacked alerts older than 5 minutes.
- Scan the change feed for any active rollouts or flagged deploys (link: Change Feed dashboard).
- Review overnight incidents summary (link: Nightly Ops Digest).
- Rehydrate local operator tooling (run: opsctl warmup) and confirm KV cache client health.
- Snapshot top-5 tenant SLO burn rates and token-burst trends.

Handoff protocol (structured, numbered):
1. Start the handoff at least 5 minutes before schedule (ideally 10).
2. Primary outgoing posts the one-line summary in #oncall-handoff channel: service, state, active pages, key actions. Example: "Handoff: Prefetch-cohort stabilization; 2 active alerts (TTL drift), no deploys in flight; secondary running prefix-cache rebalance."
3. Walk incoming through items flagged on the Pre-shift checklist and open tickets.
4. Confirm access and secrets: request verification of vault token access for operations (ops-cred-check).
5. Incoming confirms comprehension by repeating the three highest-risk items and the immediate mitigation plan.
6. Update the oncall roster board with any temporary role swaps.

Incident-continuity escalation steps (when the incident outlives the shift):
- If an incident is active near the end of shift, follow the Cross-Shift Continuity pattern:
  1) Outgoing Shift Lead writes a Situation Snapshot in the incident timeline with current hypothesis and next steps (2–3 bullets).
  2) Incoming takes 5 minutes to review the timeline artifacts and asks clarifying Qs.
  3) Responsibility transfer is documented by tagging the incident with new Primary and Secondary.
  4) If knowledge transfer requires > 30 minutes of synchronous work, schedule a follow-up detailed briefing (handoff meeting) and assign an interim runbook action.

Artifact catalog (canonical operator artifacts and minimum requirements):
- Critical runbooks (one per subsystem): must include scope, owner list, SLOs, playbook steps, and rollback criteria.
- Incident timeline template: short hypothesis, commands run, and evidence (links to traces/log queries).
- Runbook-authorship ledger: list of maintainers and last update dates.
- Training bite packets: 15–30 minute labs for platform features.

Minimum runbook metadata table (copy template into new subsystem doc):
- Name: (string)
- Service: (string)
- Owner: (name)
- Deputies: (comma-separated names)
- Critical SLOs: (comma-separated)
- Last tested: (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Runbook link: (internal link)

Critical SLIs and thresholds (operator-facing subset):
- API tail latency p99 (external primary): 500ms (SLO 99.9%)
- Token processing RT90: 300ms (SLO 99%)
- KV-prefix cache hit-rate: target > 85%
- Tenant throttling rate: < 0.2% sustained per hour
Notes: Operators should treat sustained SLO burn > 5% for more than 15 minutes as an operational escalation.

Training, certification, and drills:
- New operators complete a 4-week onboarding track: 1) fundamentals, 2) hands-on lab (synthetic incidents), 3) shadowing, 4) certification checklist.
- Quarterly tabletop drills: Knowledge Stewards run at least one session per quarter per critical subsystem.
- Annual live gameday: large-scale synthetic degradation with cross-regional failover. Postmortem feed into this playbook.

Knowledge handoff artifacts (examples):
- Minimal handoff note: "Service: router-v2 | Current state: Degraded request routing for region eu-west | Mitigation in-flight: scaled pool by +2 nodes | Next steps: validate prefix-cache rebalance and monitor p99 for 30m"
- Full handoff template (for incidents lasting > 1h): include timeline, queries used, mitigations tried, rationale for next action, named owners.

Review cadence and metrics:
- Biweekly review by platform leads of: handoff completion rate, average handoff time, and percentage of runbooks with last-tested > 90 days.
- Quarterly audit of Knowledge Steward deputies presence and documentation completeness (minimum 2 deputies per steward).

Continuous improvement workflow (how to update this playbook):
1. File a PR in the platform-runbooks repo with the proposed change and an RFC-sized description.
2. Tag Knowledge Stewards and oncall leads as reviewers.
3. Run a short pilot (one rotation) for procedural changes affecting handoff timing or escalation steps.
4. After a pilot, update the playbook and announce on #platform-ops with summary and effective date.

Backfill and long-term succession (when critical knowledge gaps are identified):
- Create a short-term shadow schedule pairing the departing steward with deputies for 4 sessions of 90 minutes each: architecture walkthrough, live ops walkthrough, runbook maintenance, and Q&A.
- Commission a permanent runbook-rotation task to rotate deputies into the steward role every 6 months for 2-week stewardship periods (documented in roster).

Runbook test matrix (recommended cadence):
- Smoke validation (basic): every 30 days
- Scenario drill (mini-gameday): every 90 days
- Full failover test: annually or prior to major regional capacity changes

Handoff: background: router-v2 rollout completed 02:20Z; current issue: region eu-west p99 elevated (720ms); mitigations: scaled router pool, started KV-prefetch restore; open tickets: #1234 (TTL rebalance). Primary outgoing: Aisha P. Incoming: Daniel K. Next check-in: +30m.
